title: Mitosis architecture audit and rebuild exploration

completion_criteria.text: Foundational audit of the current engine complete across all four domains: two-layer fan-out, durability/resume, cost/latency, pipeline rigidity + fragility
External research verdict delivered on whether the architecture is correct, with disconfirming pass and cited prior art
The child_process runtime-capability question settled empirically (does dynamic import of node:child_process EXECUTE inside a Workflow script, not merely resolve)

Three open architecture decisions resolved by the user: adopt an off-the-shelf durable-execution runtime vs only its state model; default speculation depth given that rework costs tokens not machine time; which work-type pipelines to define first
An approved architecture spec for the rebuild exists, superseding or explicitly scoping the six paused repair-oriented mitosis threads

spine.active_goal: Implement the step-6 rebuild spec. Both hand-off blockers are CLOSED: the spec is committed and pushed on docs/mitosis-core-rebuild-spec (d444797, off origin/main 6d19499) per 0129, and all five section-2 preconditions were audited by execution (0126). MSP-0 is cleared and is the whole of what step 6 can currently land; MSP-1 and every collapse MSP are blocked on absent preconditions.
spine.next_step: IMPLEMENT MSP-0 FIRST — it is cleared, the spec orders it first because it fences every later phase edit, and it depends on no precondition. Dispatch an implementer carrying 0128's corrected anchors (NEVER the spec's own line numbers), 0127's two extractor rules, and the per-write approval warning. Its falsifier is already run and survives — do not re-run it. Do NOT start MSP-1 (0126 blocks it). AFTER MSP-0, stop and re-plan: the next work is preconditions, not collapse MSPs.
open_risks: MSP-1 is BLOCKED by 0126 and cannot be unblocked inside step 6: .mitosis/run.json records no timestamp, dispatch count, wall-clock or phase entry, so there is nothing to fold. Step 3 owns the journal and must land first.
All three performance claims in spec section 14 stay labelled UNMEASURED while MSP-1 is blocked, and 0115's three falsifiers stay unpayable.

Four of five hard preconditions are NOT-LANDED, one PARTIAL (0126). Collapse MSPs 2, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 11 rest on capability that does not exist, so the spec's landing order stops dead after MSP-0. This is a defect in the plan as carried, not in the architecture.

After MSP-0 the choice is which precondition to fund. Step 1.5 is cheapest — runScheduleStreaming is built and tested, only the production flip is missing (STREAMING_DISPATCH_ENABLED = false at mitosis.js:2204, sole call site :4888-4897). Step 3 unblocks the most.

Twinning is alive, enforced by mirror-guard.test.mjs over 21 modules plus the models-knob region: any edit there must land twice byte-identically. MSP-0 is exempt — Shepherd and Final review appear in no twinned module.
Every write under .claude/{hooks,rules,lib,workflows} is held for per-write human approval, so implementers cannot be fanned out unattended. Plan interactive approval.

Spec section 15's provenance claim is false for anyone branching off main. Corrected anchors live in 0128; the spec text itself was deliberately NOT amended — amending an approved spec is the user's call.

docs/mitosis-core-rebuild-spec is pushed with NO pull request. Open it through the centralized pr-create tool.

Six other paused mitosis threads still need explicit per-thread disposition. The spec defers them rather than scoping them, which is why the last completion criterion stays unmet.
out_of_scope: Pipelines for refactor, perf, docs or chore - closed by 0118. Limits PIPELINES only, not the PR title type vocabulary.
The feat pipeline - 0110 sequences it second, after the fix pipeline proves the effector boundary and durability model against a machine-checkable oracle.
Speculation depth above 1 - 0109 requires a restack proven for the fix work type first.
Bootstrapping a target repo's test infrastructure as a side effect of shipping - closed by 0117; that is verify-setup, human-invoked.
Adopting an off-the-shelf durable-execution runtime - closed by 0108. A webhook, server or daemon for the relaunch trigger - closed by 0119.
fileScope-only task-edge derivation - rejected by 0116, settled by 0120: edges derive from a deterministic verb driving LSP over a seeded project.
Cluster-aware scheduling, and the journal's 2000-char model-output paging - real defects, but they change the scheduler and step 3 respectively; spec section 1 fences both out.
Executing the run-readiness-repair spec's 11 MSPs or quiescent-advance M0-M8, pending per-thread disposition. Dispatching or restarting any target-repo mitosis run.
